page: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-224 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the memory-optimized m4 family. It features 224 dedicated virtual CPUs and 5952.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 26.57 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage for persistent data.

From a resource density perspective, this server represents a highly specialized hardware class designed for massive memory footprints. The qualitative cost profile reflects its position as an enterprise-grade, high-capacity system where the primary value lies in consolidating massive datasets entirely in memory. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs means that workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space or hardware-accelerated parallel processing must look to alternative configurations or attach external network storage.

The m4-ultramem-224 is engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads that demand extensive memory capacity. Suitable use cases include large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, real-time data analytics, massive caching layers, and complex enterprise resource planning systems where keeping the entire working dataset in RAM is critical to performance.
